messages.content: Now match hotels to the rental plan. I need Monday night in Charlotte and Tuesday and Wednesday nights in Richmond. Charlotte has a $230 room cap before tax; Richmond is $250 before tax. Include parking and show the complete stay cost, not just nightly rates.

I found two compliant choices in each city. Before I compare them, should I optimize for the lowest total or for easier client-site access? The Richmond difference is meaningful because you will still have the one-way rental.
Balance both. This is a client trip, so keep the decision local to office access, parking, and the late arrival. Don't apply the near-beach criterion from trips with my partner here.

Understood. For Charlotte, the closest option is the Canopy SouthPark at $224 for Monday night, with $22 self-parking. At an estimated 15.25% lodging tax, the full stay is $280.16. It is about a 4-minute drive to the client office Tuesday morning. The Hampton Inn Phillips Place is $208, includes parking, and totals $239.72 with the same tax estimate. It is about a 12-minute drive in normal traffic.
Does either Charlotte rate have a cancellation deadline or destination fee?

Neither has a destination fee. The Canopy rate is refundable until 6:00 p.m. Sunday; after that, the penalty is one night. The Hampton rate is refundable until 11:59 p.m. Sunday with the same one-night penalty. Breakfast is included at the Hampton, but I have not assigned any value to that in the comparison.
So the Hampton saves a little over $40 and adds around eight minutes. Is parking definitely included for the rental, not just advertised as available?

Yes. The quoted Hampton rate includes one vehicle in its surface lot. The exact difference is $40.44 for the stay. Allowing ordinary Tuesday traffic, I would budget 12 to 18 minutes to the office rather than treating 12 minutes as guaranteed. The Canopy route is more likely to stay under 10 minutes.
Use the Hampton as the Charlotte choice. An extra eight to fourteen minutes is acceptable Tuesday morning, and the free parking makes the cost cleaner. What are the Richmond numbers?

The Richmond Marriott Downtown is the walkable option, roughly six minutes on foot from the client office. Its room rate is $246 per night for two nights, within the $250 cap. Lodging is $492, estimated 13.5% tax is $66.42, and prepaid garage parking is $30 per night, making the complete stay $618.42. The parking reservation is nonrefundable once purchased.
And the alternative with free parking?

The Courtyard Richmond West is $232 per night on a refundable rate. Two nights are $464, estimated tax is $62.64, and parking is included, for a complete stay of $526.64. It is about an 18-minute drive to the office without congestion; for the Wednesday morning meeting I would plan on 25 to 35 minutes. Thursday's departure is less sensitive because you can leave after the client session.
Check the late-arrival issue against both. The rental plan gets me to Richmond around 10:10 Tuesday, but the stress case was 11:20, and we already noted a call after pickup.

The Marriott desk is staffed overnight, and the garage entrance remains open, but prepaid parking needs the vehicle details entered before arrival. The Courtyard also has overnight desk coverage and does not require advance parking registration. Either removes the midnight-desk concern that applied to the earlier hotel candidate, though calling after rental pickup is still sensible if the drive slips.
Is the Marriott room itself refundable? I don't want the parking wording to hide a prepaid room rate.

The $246 Marriott room rate is refundable until 6:00 p.m. Monday. Only the $60 garage reservation is prepaid and nonrefundable. The Courtyard's $232 rate can be canceled until 6:00 p.m. Monday as well, with no parking payment at risk.
Compare the Richmond options in practical terms. Include the total difference and the driving burden over both client days.

The Marriott costs $91.78 more overall: $618.42 versus $526.64. It avoids the Wednesday morning drive and lets you walk about six minutes to the office. You would likely drive only when leaving Richmond Thursday. The Courtyard adds one inbound office trip Wednesday and another Thursday, approximately 36 minutes total in light traffic or 50 to 70 minutes with morning congestion. It also avoids the nonrefundable $60 parking commitment and is simpler for a late arrival.
The Thursday meeting starts at 8:30 too, so count that as two morning drives. With that correction, which would you choose?

With 8:30 starts on both days, I would choose the Marriott. The $91.78 premium buys two walkable mornings, avoids two congestion-sensitive drives, and keeps the rental parked until Thursday departure. Its $246 room rate still complies with the Richmond cap. The tradeoff is the prepaid $60 garage charge, so I would not purchase parking until the intercity rental is reserved.
Agreed. Retain the Hampton in Charlotte and the Marriott in Richmond. Give me the combined lodging amount and make sure nothing is booked yet.

The retained lodging plan is the Hampton Inn Phillips Place for Monday at $239.72 complete, and the Richmond Marriott Downtown for Tuesday and Wednesday at $618.42 complete. Combined lodging is $858.14, including estimated lodging taxes and all parking charges. The room rates are $208 in Charlotte and $246 per night in Richmond, so both satisfy their before-tax limits. Nothing has been booked, and the Marriott garage payment should wait until the one-way rental is reserved.
